results.label: scam
results.text: Hello Mr. Johnson, this is Karen from the Medicare benefits review office. We are updating records for members in your county and just need to confirm your Medicare number. You can call me back at 602-555-0171 whenever convenient.
results.summary: This is an impersonation scam pretending to be Medicare to steal your Medicare number and identity.

results.label: scam
results.text: Hi, our billing system refunded you $2,990 instead of $299 by mistake. Could you please send back the $2,691 difference using a Walmart money transfer today? Thank you for helping us fix this.
results.summary: This is a classic overpayment/refund scam asking you to return a fake over-refund via an irreversible Walmart money transfer.

results.label: scam
results.text: Thanks for applying! We would love to move you forward as a data entry assistant. The interview will be done over Google Chat. Before we start, please send a photo of your driver's license and your SSN for the background check.
results.summary: This is a fake job / identity-theft scam — no real employer asks for a photo of your driver's license and Social Security Number over Google Chat before an interview.

results.label: scam
results.text: Hi tenants, we have changed our banking provider. Starting this month please send rent by Zelle to our new account at pm.rentoffice2026@gmail.com. The old account is closed. Thanks!
results.summary: This is a payment-diversion scam impersonating your property manager to reroute rent payments to a new Zelle Gmail address.

results.label: scam
results.text: Hello, this is Dana at Hartley Title. Please note our wire instructions have changed for your closing on Friday. Updated routing and account numbers are attached. Kindly wire the $48,200 down payment by Thursday noon.
results.summary: This is a real-estate wire-fraud scam impersonating Hartley Title to get you to wire $48,200 to new account numbers.

results.label: scam
results.text: Hi Accounts Payable, please update our remittance details for invoice #7741. Our new bank information is attached. Kindly confirm once changed and process the $12,480 payment this week.
results.summary: This is a classic Business Email Compromise request to hijack a vendor payment by changing bank details for a $12,480 invoice.

results.label: scam
results.text: We are a licensed digital asset recovery firm. Our records show you may have lost funds in a crypto platform failure. For a small upfront retainer of $450 we can recover up to 95% of your funds.
results.summary: This is an advance-fee crypto recovery scam asking for $450 upfront while promising to recover 95% of lost funds.

results.label: scam
results.text: Congratulations, you have been selected to receive a $9,000 federal community grant. There is nothing to repay. A $150 verification fee by prepaid card is required to release the funds.
results.summary: This is an advance-fee grant scam impersonating a federal program: real U.S. federal grants never require a prepaid card fee to release money.

results.label: scam
results.text: We've been trying to reach you about your vehicle's extended warranty. Your coverage is about to lapse. Please call 888-555-0166 so we can go over your options.
results.summary: This is the classic unsolicited 'vehicle extended warranty about to lapse' robocall scam that tries to pressure you into calling back and sharing personal/payment information.

results.label: scam
results.text: Hi mum, I dropped my phone in the sink and this is my new number. Can you save it? Also can you help me pay a bill today, my banking app is locked.
results.summary: This is the well-known 'Hi mum' scam where someone pretends to be your child on a new number and asks you to pay a bill because their banking app is locked.

results.label: scam
results.text: Hey! Long time no see. I started trading with this platform my aunt recommended and made a decent profit last month, happy to show you how it works if you're curious. No pressure!
results.summary: This is a casual, low-pressure chat message offering to show a trading platform with no link, payment request, or personal data request.

results.label: scam
results.text: Your package from Amazon could not be delivered because the address is incomplete. Please reply with your full address and the card on file so we can reship.
results.summary: This is a fake Amazon delivery message trying to steal your address and payment card details by asking you to reply by text.

results.label: scam
results.text: Your electric company has moved to a new online payment portal. To avoid any interruption of service, please re-enter your payment details at the new portal by Friday: https://srp-billing-portal.com/login
results.summary: This message impersonates your electric company and directs you to a fake billing portal to steal payment details.

results.label: scam
results.text: Hello, I am calling from Banner Health. Your brother was admitted after an accident and needs a deposit before surgery. Can you wire $3,000 right now? I can give you the account number.
results.summary: This is a classic family-emergency impersonation scam claiming to be Banner Health to pressure you into wiring $3,000 — real U.S. hospitals do not demand wire transfers by phone before emergency surgery.

results.label: scam
results.text: Hi Linda, this is Bob from Publishers Prize Patrol. You have won $1.2 million and a new Mercedes! Before we deliver the prize we just need you to cover the $890 insurance and tax in advance.
results.summary: This is a classic prize scam impersonating the Publishers Clearing House Prize Patrol — real sweepstakes never make you pay insurance or taxes in advance to receive a prize.

results.label: scam
results.text: This is a courtesy reminder from the Internal Revenue Service. You are eligible for a reduced settlement of your tax debt. To lock in the discount please call 480-555-0144 and have a payment method ready.
results.summary: This is a fake IRS text trying to get you to call and pay - the real IRS doesn't contact you this way about settlements.

results.label: scam
results.text: Honey, my business trip hit a problem and my account is frozen here. Can you help me with $1,500 for the hotel until my bank fixes it? I will pay you back as soon as I'm home, I promise.
results.summary: This is an unverifiable emergency money request claiming to be someone close to you ("Honey") who is stranded — a setup used in many impersonation and family-emergency scams.

results.label: scam
results.text: Your annual subscription of $499.99 for Norton 360 has been renewed and will be charged to your card. If you want to cancel, our support desk at 1-844-555-0112 will assist you with the refund.
results.summary: Unsolicited Norton 360 renewal for $499.99 asking you to call 1-844-555-0112 for a refund is the classic Norton refund/callback scam.

results.label: scam
results.text: Hi, this is Tom from your bank's fraud team. We've noticed some transfers on your account. To protect your money we need you to move your funds to a temporary safe account. I'll guide you through it.
results.summary: Message impersonates a bank fraud team and asks you to move money to a so-called "safe account" — a classic scam no real bank ever uses.

results.label: scam
results.text: This is the Office of Student Aid. Your account shows an unclaimed refund of $1,832. To release it please confirm your bank login and student ID on our secure page.
results.summary: Message impersonates the Office of Student Aid and tries to steal your bank login with a fake $1,832 refund.

results.label: legit
results.text: Chase: We locked your card ending 4421 after unusual activity. Call the number on the back of your card or visit chase.com/fraud. We will never ask for your PIN or full card number.
results.summary: This is a legitimate Chase fraud alert on its official domain that tells you to use the number on your card and does not ask for your PIN or full card number.

results.label: legit
results.text: Arizona MVD: Your vehicle registration expires in 5 days. Renew online at azmvdnow.gov to avoid a late fee. Reply STOP to opt out.
results.summary: This looks like a normal Arizona MVD registration reminder pointing to the official AZ MVD Now government site.

results.label: legit
results.text: Reminder from Cactus Ridge Apartments: rent is due on the 1st and a late fee applies after the 5th. Pay through the resident portal you already use.
results.summary: This is a generic rent reminder with no link, code request, or payment demand, just directing you to use your existing resident portal.

results.label: legit
results.text: Verizon: Your account is past due $87.30. To avoid service suspension on Nov 3, pay at verizon.com/myverizon or in the My Verizon app.
results.summary: This is a standard Verizon bill reminder directing you to the official Verizon website and app to pay.

results.label: legit
results.text: ASU IT: Your password expires in 2 days. Change it at the ASU password page you reach through your MyASU account. IT will never ask for your password by email.
results.summary: This is a routine password-expiry reminder that directs you to use your official MyASU account and explicitly says IT will never ask for your password by email, with no link, payment, or code request.

results.label: legit
results.text: USPS: Final notice. Your package could not be delivered and is being held at the Mesa Post Office through Nov 2. Bring a photo ID to pick it up.
results.summary: This is a simple in-person pickup notice with no link, payment request, or request for personal info — just to bring ID to the post office.

results.label: legit
results.text: Banner Health: Your lab results are ready. Log in to your patient portal to view them. If you need help, call the number on your appointment card.
results.summary: This is a standard lab-results notification with no link, no payment request, and it correctly tells you to use your patient portal and the number on your appointment card.

results.label: legit
results.text: Capital One: Did you make a $212.40 purchase at BEST BUY on Oct 25 with your card ending 1034? Reply YES or NO. We'll never ask for your full card number.
results.summary: This is a normal Capital One fraud check asking for a simple YES/NO to confirm a Best Buy transaction, with no link and explicitly not asking for your full card number.

results.label: legit
results.text: Coinbase: New sign-in from Chrome on macOS in Phoenix. If this was you, no action needed. If not, secure your account at coinbase.com/security.
results.summary: This appears to be a standard Coinbase security notification directing you to their official website (coinbase.com/security), with no request for passwords, seed phrase, or funds.

results.label: legit
results.text: Your Apple ID was used to sign in to iMessage on a new Mac. If this was you, you can ignore this message. If not, change your password at appleid.apple.com.
results.summary: This is a normal informational alert about an Apple ID sign-in, pointing to Apple's real website appleid.apple.com, with no scam indicators.

results.label: legit
results.text: Medicare: Open enrollment ends Dec 7. Review your plan options at medicare.gov/plan-compare. Medicare will never call you to sell a plan or ask for your number.
results.summary: Legitimate informational message pointing to the official Medicare website (medicare.gov) with accurate advice about Medicare not calling to sell plans.

results.label: legit
results.text: URGENT from Desert View High: Early dismissal today at 12:30 due to a power outage. Please arrange pickup. Buses will run on the revised schedule.
results.summary: This is a routine school information notice about early dismissal with no links, payment requests, or requests for personal information.

results.label: legit
results.text: PayPal: You received $50.00 USD from Alex Chen. The money is in your PayPal balance. See details at paypal.com/activity.
results.summary: This looks like a standard PayPal notification that you received $50, with a link to PayPal's real website to view your activity.

results.label: legit
results.text: Amazon: Your order #112-4488201 needs your attention: the delivery address couldn't be verified. Update it in Your Orders at amazon.com/your-orders within 24 hours.
results.summary: This looks like a normal Amazon order notice directing you to the official amazon.com Your Orders page, with no signs of impersonation or fraud.

results.label: legit
results.text: Geico: Your payment of $184.20 was declined. Your policy may lapse on Nov 1 if payment is not received. Update your payment method at geico.com or in the Geico app.
results.summary: The message directs you to the real GEICO website (geico.com) and app to update a declined payment — it does not use a lookalike link, gift card, or request for codes.

results.label: legit
results.text: Subject: IRS: Your Notice CP14 for tax year 2025 is available. Read it at irs.gov and review your payment options. The IRS will never demand payment by gift card or crypto.
results.summary: Message directs to the official irs.gov domain with ordinary notice information and explicitly warns against gift card/crypto demands, matching IRS policy.

results.text: SRP: Your account is 45 days past due ($212.18). Service may be disconnected on Nov 10. Pay at srpnet.com or call the number on your bill to set up a payment plan.
results.summary: This appears to be a routine SRP utility bill reminder pointing to the official srpnet.com website and telling you to use the number on your bill, not a scam number or link.

results.label: legit
results.text: Bank of America: Your online banking was accessed from a new device. If this was you, no action is needed. If not, call the number on the back of your card. We'll never ask for your passcode.
results.summary: This is a standard security notice that tells you to use the official number on your card and never share your passcode, with no link or request for personal information.

results.label: legit
results.text: Subject: Action required: complete your I-9 verification by Friday. Bring your documents to the HR office in Tempe, 2nd floor, or use the HR portal you were given at orientation.
results.summary: This is a routine HR reminder to complete I-9 verification in person or via a portal you already have, with no link, payment, or code request.

results.summary: This appears to be a routine subscription reminder that correctly directs you to Spotify's official website and app.
